_comment: BRAND REGISTRY v1.0. Identical in every brand kit. One place that knows every brand in the house. An agent reads this to resolve a brand name to its CDN root, palette, tokens and logo files without knowing per-brand filenames. Adding a brand means adding one entry here plus the files it points at. See NEW-BRAND.md.

shared._comment: Identical in every kit. Served from the parent brand because the type layer belongs to Collective Edge and is inherited down.

cobrand._comment: POWERED BY COLLECTIVE EDGE. Identical in every kit. The shipped co-brand lockup, captured from apex-website/src/components/Footer.astro, web-apex-internal-dashboard/src/components/Sidebar.astro and apex-customer-dashboard/src/components/Sidebar.astro. An agent resolves the lockup, the width and the placement rules from here rather than reinventing a treatment. CSS: snippets/cobrand.css, identical in every kit and served from the parent brand.
cobrand.label: Powered by
cobrand.documents: documents.json cobrand holds the document lockup and the placement for each document type. In a PDF, a deck or an image the lockup is small: the words Powered by at caption size, then the Collective Edge horizontal logo at its 120px minimum, 1.25in, on one line. A working-doc and a sheet never carry it. The 204px values below are for sites and dashboards

lockup.widthNote: 204px is the shipped width in both the Apex website footer and the Apex internal dashboard sidebar. It is sized to read at a glance rather than sit quietly in a corner, which is why it runs wider than the partner mark above it. The 120px minimum in the Collective Edge kit is a floor, not a target. max-width:100% is the only thing that takes it below 204px, and only where the rail is narrower.
lockup.fileRule: Match the file to the background. White on dark, black on light. Never CSS-filter a logo to invert it.

hairline.rule: The CE lockup rides beside the partner brand, never inside it, so a hairline keeps the two marks distinct. The two read as two brands rather than one combined mark.
hairline.geometry: margin-top and padding-top --space-5 (24px), label to lockup gap --space-3 (12px)

labelType.surfaceNote: The light lockup belongs on --bg-canvas, not on --bg-surface. On the tinted surface the same gray measures 4.53:1 for Collective Edge, 4.64:1 for Apex and 4.76:1 for Royal. On --bg-surface-2 it falls to 4.10:1, 4.27:1 and 4.12:1, under 4.5:1.

placement: The sidebar header of any dashboard
The footer row of the closing slide of a deck, small
The footer row of a memo or a one-pager, on page 1, small
The last line of a report body, small
A data page or a methodology page
Anywhere a number was computed rather than typed
doNot: Put it on the partner's own mark or inside their lockup
Merge, nest or recolor either mark to match the other
Put it on a clinical instruction
Put it on a patient-facing consent or safety document
Use it twice in one document or on one surface
Set the phrase as type where the mark fits. A chart or data graphic made on its own is the one place the words stand alone
Design the lockup down to the 120px floor on a site or a dashboard
Set it larger than 1.25in in a PDF, a deck or an image
Put it on a working document or a sheet, as a lockup or as words

logoRoles._comment: Every brand maps the horizontal and mark roles. Ask for a role, never for a filename. `-on-light` means the version to place ON a light background; `-on-dark` the version to place ON a dark background. The compact pair, the stacked pair and the app icon are optional: present where a brand ships one, null or absent where it does not. logosPng in each brand holds the same roles as PNG.
logoRoles.compact-on-light: the short lockup, for smaller places, decks, or a corner, light backgrounds
logoRoles.compact-on-dark: the short lockup, for smaller places, decks, or a corner, dark backgrounds
logoRoles.stacked-on-light: optional vertical lockup, light backgrounds; null when the brand has none
logoRoles.stacked-on-dark: optional vertical lockup, dark backgrounds; null when the brand has none
logoRoles.app-icon: the mark on its own square, for favicons and app tiles; null when the brand has none

collective-edge.name: Collective Edge
collective-edge.colorNote: Collective Edge has no hue of its own. It reads as tiers: black for the hero and the accent, graphite #23232A for the band and the body ink, #4E4F58 for the mid tone, then two tints and white. On a co-brand surface the Edge wedge takes the PARTNER's hue.

logosPng._comment: The same roles as transparent PNG, for Word, PowerPoint and Google files. Each also ships at double width: 2400w for 1200w, 1024w for 512w.

cobrandMarks._comment: The Edge wedge carries the partner's hue. Every combination ships as a file. Never hand-recolor a mark.

heroTreatment._comment: Collective Edge signature. Apex and Royal do not use it; their dark bands are flat brand color. Title slides, section dividers and the marketing hero only, once per surface. Never behind body copy, never on an internal document. Not used in a document or a deck built from reference/layout.md. Those slides are flat #000000.

slideBackground._comment: Scrim already composited. Drop straight onto a PowerPoint or Keynote slide as a picture background. No CSS, no further work.

safeZonesForReversedType._comment: Worst-pixel contrast against #FFFFFF, measured on the shipped asset. The wave puts its light upper-left.

apex.name: Apex Paramedics
apex.colorNote: Blue is the structure, gold is the spark. Bright gold #FDB61C measures 1.77:1 on white and fails contrast as text there. Use #B77808, and only at bold or large sizes. Gold is a brand accent, never a status color.

logosPng._comment: The same roles as transparent PNG, for Word, PowerPoint and Google files. Each also ships at double width: 2400w for 1200w, 1024w for 512w.

apex.logoNote: The main logo is APEX PARAMEDICS, the horizontal lockup. The compact lockup is APEX alone, for smaller places, decks, or a corner. The mark is the A with the gold arc running through it, for favicons, avatars and any space too small for the compact lockup; app-icon.svg is the same mark on a navy square. The gold arc never appears without a letter: the arc-only files mark-color.svg and mark-white.svg are deleted, and scripts/validate.py fails on any reference to them. The delivered compact files carried #000F9F and #FFB71B; both are normalised to the primary lockup so the house ships one blue and one gold. The delivered originals are in the git history, at the commit that adopted the set.

royal.name: Royal Ambulance
royal.colorNote: Purple is the whole palette. #43205b is the logo fill. Light purple #8260a2 is for tertiary accents and hover only, never text on white.

logosPng._comment: The same roles as transparent PNG, for Word, PowerPoint and Google files. Each also ships at double width: 2400w for 1200w, 1024w for 512w.

diagramRoles._comment: Functional colors for flowcharts, status and dashboards. Identical across every brand so a diagram reads the same regardless of whose document it sits in. The fills are the alert and neutral families in each palette.css. Never invent new hues for these roles. A brand accent is never a status color. Each role names the text color that clears contrast on it; measured, do not substitute.

warning.textRule: ink, not white. White on this amber measures 3.40:1 and fails at body size.

diagramRoles.shape: rectangles, 6px radius. Role is communicated by fill color, never by shape.

unreconciled._comment: No brand kit exists for these. Inherited from an original design export and NOT verified against a source of truth. Confirm before use in anything shipping.
